rubric.why: Newlands arranged elements in order of increasing atomic mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the elements were arranged in order of increasing atomic mass or atomic weight.

rubric.why: In this arrangement, every eighth element had properties similar to the first.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that every eighth element had properties similar to the first.

modelAnswer: Newlands arranged the elements in order of increasing atomic masses.
He observed that every eighth element had properties similar to the first, like notes in an octave.

items.followUp: Give one example of a measurement whose SI unit is the metre.

rubric.why: Atomic radius is defined by the distance from an atom’s nucleus to its outermost electron shell, or equivalently half the distance between adjacent nuclei.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of atomic radius.

rubric.why: The SI unit of length, and therefore of atomic radius, is the metre.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius is the distance from the centre of an atom’s nucleus to its outermost electron shell.
Its SI unit is the metre (m).

items.followUp: Explain how a coordinate covalent bond forms in the hydronium ion, H₃O⁺.

rubric.why: Nitrogen in ammonia has a lone pair of electrons available for donation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the lone pair on nitrogen in NH₃.

rubric.why: Nitrogen donates its lone pair to H⁺, forming the coordinate bond in NH₄⁺.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the lone pair is donated to H⁺ to form a coordinate covalent bond.

modelAnswer: The nitrogen atom in NH₃ has a lone pair of electrons.
It donates this pair to H⁺, forming a coordinate covalent bond and producing NH₄⁺.

items.followUp: Give two differences between ionic and covalent compounds.

rubric.why: Polar compounds have an unequal charge distribution and a dipole; nonpolar compounds do not have a permanent dipole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting the charge distribution or dipole of polar and nonpolar compounds.

rubric.why: The solubility of each type generally follows the polarity of the solvent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that polar compounds generally dissolve in polar solvents and nonpolar compounds in nonpolar solvents.

modelAnswer: Polar compounds have partial positive and negative ends (a dipole); nonpolar compounds do not have a permanent dipole.
Polar compounds generally dissolve in polar solvents, whereas nonpolar compounds generally dissolve in nonpolar solvents.
